A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DACA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated sections and displays.

before.justification: v2 reports original calibration experiments across multiple LLMs on MMLU, MedMCQA, MathQA and TruthfulQA in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix D, including open-ended QA and selective-classification evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same agreement-only KL alignment objective, temperature optimization and vector/matrix scaling extensions. Equations (7)–(8) introduce no procedural change between versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, MedMCQA, MathQA and TruthfulQA, including open-ended QA and selective classification. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including CAPE, Elicitation, Elicitation-Ensemble and supervised TS/VS/MS references where reported.

E3.justification: Both retain the same model configurations, metrics, ten ECE bins, subject-specific MMLU validation sets and 7:3 test-to-validation splitting elsewhere. Calibration training settings and open-ended QA testing procedures also match.

E4.justification: The agreement/disagreement temperature analysis, additional reliability diagrams, and analyses of model size, PLM choice and post-training strategy are retained. Figures 2 and 6–8 and the corresponding appendix analyses contain no new tests.

E5.justification: Both disclose five prompt variants for MMLU and five random splits for other datasets, with mean and standard-deviation reporting. Run information and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched tables and plotted findings retain the same results. For example, DACA's Gemma-3-12B-Instruct ECE remains 8.596±0.380% in Table 1, and its Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct TruthfulQA ECE remains 5.244±0.804% in Table 12.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Propositions 3.2–3.3 and their mathematical arguments are unchanged. The existing proofs move from Appendix C in v2 to Appendix B in v5 without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims concerning unlabeled calibration, disagreement-aware alignment, broad LLM applicability, open-ended QA and selective classification.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanation that disagreement can drive excessive temperatures and under-confidence. The limitations concerning additional PLM inference and the reduced calibration pool after filtering disagreement examples are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware/software disclosures, Adam settings, prompt templates, data-processing instructions and code-access information are unchanged. Implementation details move from Appendix D to Appendix C; the new acknowledgment adds no reproducibility settings.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited-work membership are unchanged after relocation from Appendix A to Section 6. An existing Tao et al. reference gains an arXiv identifier, which is a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: v5 moves related work into the main text and places the checklist before the appendices, updating section references accordingly. It also adds acknowledgments and changes the author name from Yixuan Li to Sharon Li; scientific prose is otherwise essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: All eight figures and twelve tables are retained with unchanged visual content and table structures. Limited layout changes relocate Table 4, split Figures 6–7 across pages and reflow appendix discussion and floats.

improvement.justification: v5 primarily reorganizes existing material and adds acknowledgments and metadata edits. The method, proofs, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations and reproducibility documentation remain unchanged, so these limited editorial adjustments produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
